Both incidents took place on Millhouse Woods Lane, the road that leads to Hull's training ground. The road has a speed limit of 30 mph (48 kph). Humberside Police said police and emergency services attended a traffic collision on Thursday involving a single vehicle at 8:30 a.m. and there were no injuries. The 23-year-old Gourna-Douath's car was on its side after the accident, The Telegraph said. Hull's Wales winger Thomas, 27, emerged "completely unscathed" after an [USN:L4N4530VE TEXT:"accident on September 11"], with images showing his car upside down on a small residential road. Reuters has contacted Hull for comment. The promoted side have had an encouraging start to the season and stand in eighth place in the Premier League. They next host Everton on October 11.

item.title: Sudan's ousted president Bashir sent to Khartoum for treatment, lawyer says
item.description: Ousted Sudanese President Omar al-Bashir has been transferred to a military-run hospital in Khartoum for medical treatment and requires further care outside the country, his lawyer said on Thursday.
item.dc:creator: Khalid Abdelaziz
item.content:encoded: Ousted Sudanese President Omar al-Bashir has been transferred to a military-run hospital in Khartoum for medical treatment and requires further care outside the country, his lawyer said on Thursday. Bashir, 82, was toppled by the Sudanese army and the paramilitary Rapid Support Forces in April 2019, following a months-long popular uprising. The RSF and army later fell out over plans to integrate their forces during a planned transition to civilian rule and have been fighting a civil war that has [USN:L6N45M0KU TEXT:"laid waste"] to much of the country over the past three-and-a-half years. Bashir had been moved from prison to hospital prior to the outbreak of war, and [USN:C6N325021 TEXT:"later transferred"] to the town of Merowe in northern Sudan, where he had been put under military guard. Bashir was sent to Khartoum for medical tests and he had symptoms that required diagnosis and treatment outside Sudan, his lawyer, Mohamed Alhassan Alameen, told Reuters. In a statement on Wednesday, Bashir's family said his need for medical treatment outside Sudan "has become critical and urgent, and cannot be delayed any longer", but they had not received official permission to send him abroad. It was unclear precisely what condition Bashir was suffering. Sudan's military did not immediately respond to a request for comment. Several prominent [USN:L1N3TM0V6 TEXT:"Sudanese Islamist figures"] also called for his transfer out of the country on social media. Any such move would likely cause discord within Sudan and could draw international condemnation since [USN:L6N3VN0KH TEXT:"Bashir is wanted"] by the International Criminal Court on charges including genocide and also has open cases against him in Sudan. During Bashir's three decades in power, Sudan was listed by the US as a state sponsor of terrorism and was subject to wide-ranging sanctions. Protesters during the popular uprising accused him and his Islamist National Congress Party of widespread corruption and repression. After his ouster, Bashir was tried on various charges and convicted of corruption and illicit financing, for which he was serving prison time at the start of the war.

item.title: Hackers chinos se hicieron pasar por exfuncionaria de EEUU para robar correos electrónicos sobre IA
item.description: Unos hackers chinos se hicieron pasar por expertos estadounidenses en inteligencia artificial, entre ellos una antigua funcionaria del Gobierno, para intentar robar correos electrónicos a expertos de centros de estudios, universidades y otras organizaciones, según informó el jueves la empresa de ciberseguridad Proofpoint.
item.dc:creator: Raphael Satter, A.J. Vicens
item.content:encoded: Unos hackers chinos se hicieron pasar por expertos estadounidenses en inteligencia artificial, entre ellos una antigua funcionaria del Gobierno, para intentar robar correos electrónicos a expertos de centros de estudios, universidades y otras organizaciones, según informó el jueves la empresa de ciberseguridad Proofpoint. En un informe, Proofpoint señaló que había observado cómo los hackers —a los que denomina "TA419"— intentan robar contraseñas de forma regular a personas que trabajan para centros de estudios, empresas de defensa, universidades y bufetes de abogados de Estados Unidos o Japón desde el año 2025. Proofpoint atribuyó estos ataques al grupo chino basándose en los tipos de malware utilizados, la infraestructura de Internet empleada para llevar a cabo los ataques y los objetivos en los que observó que se centraba el grupo, que coinciden con las prioridades de recopilación de información de los servicios de inteligencia chinos. Proofpoint señaló que la reciente campaña de los hackers consistía en redactar correos electrónicos que fingían proceder de expertos en IA o en asuntos de Estado, entre ellos Lynne Parker, quien anteriormente trabajó como subdirectora principal de la Oficina de Política Científica y Tecnológica de la Casa Blanca. Proofpoint indicó que los correos electrónicos solían proponer colaboraciones o iniciativas relacionadas con la IA antes de dirigir a los destinatarios hacia sitios web destinados a robar contraseñas. La embajada china en Washington no respondió de inmediato a un mensaje en el que se le solicitaban comentarios. Pekín lleva mucho tiempo negando que lleve a cabo operaciones de ciberespionaje. Proofpoint se negó a revelar los nombres de los objetivos de los piratas informáticos, limitándose a indicar que entre ellos se encontraban "expertos que trabajan en la regulación de la IA, los controles de exportación y la estrategia nacional de IA". Reuters pudo identificar de forma independiente a uno de ellos: Alex Engler, un exfuncionario de la Casa Blanca que ahora dirige el Penn Center on Media, Technology, and Democracy. Engler dijo el miércoles a Reuters que había recibido un correo electrónico que parecía proceder de Parker y en el que se le invitaba "a unirse a un nuevo proyecto sobre políticas de IA". Sin embargo, señaló que "le pareció un poco extraño, vagamente sospechoso" y, tras consultarlo con varios colegas, constató que era un impostor. Parker declaró a Reuters que Engler era una de las dos personas de las que tenía constancia que habían recibido mensajes sospechosos que supuestamente procedían de ella a principios de julio. Añadió que la acusación de implicación china tenía sentido. "Estados Unidos y China compiten en el ámbito de la IA", afirmó Parker. "Intentar que personas del ámbito de la política de IA revelen información sobre sus planes en materia de IA —si es que ese era realmente el objetivo— no es nada sorprendente".

item.title: Japón y Ecuador igualan sin goles en segundo encuentro de DT Gallardo al mando del combinado sudamericano
item.description: Las selecciones de fútbol de Japón y Ecuador igualaron sin goles el jueves, en un partido amistoso que se definió a favor del equipo japonés tras lanzamientos penales, en el segundo encuentro del argentino Marcelo Gallardo al mando del combinado sudamericano.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Las selecciones de fútbol de Japón y Ecuador igualaron sin goles el jueves, en un partido amistoso que se definió a favor del equipo japonés tras lanzamientos penales, en el segundo encuentro del argentino Marcelo Gallardo al mando del combinado sudamericano. Gallardo trató de corregir los errores comentidos por la selección en el primer partido de su era, que culminó con una categórica derrota de 3-0 a manos de Corea del Sur la semana pasada. Durante el partido, Ecuador tuvo más tiempo el balón con un juego con pases largos y por los extremos, pero no logró anotar. Gallardo realizó varios cambios en el medio campo para modificar el juego colectivo. Mientras, a Japón le faltó profundidad para complicar al arquero del equipo andino Hernán Galíndez, aunque aumentó la presión sobre la salida ecuatoriana en el segundo tiempo del encuentro, que se jugó en el Estadio Internacional de Yokohama. En la fase de penales, el arquero Zion Suzuki atajó un tiro del ecuatoriano Denil Castillo, dando el triunfo 5-4 a su equipo. Gallardo fue designado técnico de Ecuador el 13 de septiembre en sustitución de Sebastián Beccacece, quien en julio renunció tras perder por 2-0 ante México en los dieciseisavos de final de la reciente Copa del Mundo. El estratega argentino ha prometido trabajar para que la selección de fútbol dé un salto de calidad y tenga la convicción del potencial que tiene de cara al próximo Mundial.

item.title: Europe's defence spending props up shrinking refining sector, says VAROPreem CEO
item.description: Europe's shrinking oil refining sector is benefiting from rising demand for the fuel needed to support government defence plans, the CEO of one of the continent's biggest refiners said.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Europe's shrinking oil refining sector is benefiting from rising demand for the fuel needed to support government defence plans, the CEO of one of the continent's biggest refiners said. European Union member states' defence spending rose for the 11th year running in 2025 to €418 billion ($472 billion), marking a 75% increase since 2021, with further gains forecast for this year, data from the European Council shows. "Every conversation I'm having with European governments today is all about how do you maintain resilience, how do you maintain continuity of supply? I would say that period between 2015 and 2022 the entire focus was how could you shut refineries down," VAROPreem CEO Dev Sanyal told Reuters on Thursday. "European governments realise that there's a need for more fuel. There's (also) a need for more energy because of the competitive advantage Europe wants to achieve on AI," he added. Since 2009, 30 of around 100 refineries operating in Europe have been closed or converted and at least seven converted into biorefineries, severely curbing the capacity to produce diesel, gasoline or jet fuel in the European Union, Britain, Norway and Switzerland, a report by trade group FuelsEurope said. "Now, with defence spending, you realise that whether you have F-35s (US-made fighter jets), you have Leopard tanks, they don't run on biogas," said the CEO of Swiss-headquartered VAROPreem, which has a capacity of around 530,000 barrels per day with refineries in Sweden, Switzerland and Germany. Refining capacity in EU countries, Britain, Turkey, Ukraine and Switzerland stood at 14.4 million bpd last year, down from 17.5 million bpd in 2009, according to the Statistical Review of World Energy most recently published by the Energy Institute. Diesel prices have rocketed since the Iran war choked off vital shipping lanes and following sustained attacks on Russian refining infrastructure. The benchmark European diesel futures contract has hit highs above $14 a metric ton since the Iran war began, levels last seen in the aftermath of Russia's invasion of Ukraine in 2022. Meanwhile, US retail diesel prices hit a [USN:L6N45M0ZI TEXT:"record $6.50"] per gallon this month, with [USN:L6N45N0GM TEXT:"US pressure"] on Europe to release diesel stockpiles rising, sources said. ($1 = 0.8851 euros)

item.title: Netanyahu dice que el copiloto de flydubai fue sometido a un adoctrinamiento radical islamista
item.description: El primer ministro israelí, Benjamin Netanyahu, afirmó el jueves que el copiloto que intentó estrellar un avión de pasajeros que se dirigía a Israel había sufrido un proceso de radicalización islamista.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: El primer ministro israelí, Benjamin Netanyahu, afirmó el jueves que el copiloto que intentó estrellar un avión de pasajeros que se dirigía a Israel había sufrido un proceso de radicalización islamista. "Sabemos que fue sometido a un adoctrinamiento radical islamista", declaró Netanyahu en una entrevista con Fox News. Aún no se ha determinado el motivo del angustioso incidente que estuvo a punto de provocar una catástrofe el miércoles en el vuelo FZ1073 de flydubai, que cubría la ruta de Dubái a Tel Aviv, en el que los pasajeros lograron reducir al agresor y la tripulación de reserva a bordo aterrizó el avión en Arabia Saudita . Netanyahu declaró en el programa Fox & Friends que en cuestión de días podría confirmar si el copiloto de flydubai tenía vínculos con Irán. "Creo que es demasiado pronto para decir si tenía alguna conexión con Irán o con cualquier otra persona", afirmó. Netanyahu señaló que estaba claro que el copiloto tenía tendencias suicidas. "Si a eso le sumamos lo que acabo de comentarles sobre las tendencias islamistas y la radicalización que se aprecian en sus antecedentes, creo que eso nos dará una pista bastante clara", señaló. "Pero, insisto, aún no saco conclusiones definitivas. No obstante, ésas son las indicaciones de las que disponemos por ahora".

item.title: Brazil laudably ups the ante on betting crackdowns
item.description: President Lula wants to ban some $7 bln of legal online gambling, seizing on populist backlash as he seeks reelection. Black markets are a problem, but less so than the associated health effects and societal costs. As awareness spreads, so will tougher policies and prohibitions.
item.dc:creator: Jeffrey Goldfarb
item.content:encoded: All politics is local, but gambling troubles are global. It’s what makes the bold decision by Brazilian President Luiz Inacio Lula da Silva to outlaw online betting so compelling. In a bid to help his reelection campaign, he seized on populist backlash and reversed himself just a few years after authorizing the addictive activity. In doing so, his country will accelerate worldwide policy conversations about a spreading health epidemic. Ballot boxes and stock markets provide early barometers. Brazilians, who will [USN:L1N45G04J TEXT:"cast their votes"] in a close race on Sunday, made their concerns clear: 75% of those polled recently backed an online betting ban. Local site operators, including Entain and Flutter Entertainment, will suffer from the license revocations in a promising $7 billion growth market . Allwyn scrapped its earlier profit margin guidance following the executive order. Lula’s radical course of action, which faces a legal challenge and requires congressional approval to stay in place, also speaks to otherwise tepid regulatory responses. It has been two years since an international panel convened by medical journal Lancet flagged that the damage to public health and wellbeing from gambling, including suicide and domestic violence, is “more substantial than previously understood.” Sophisticated marketing and betting on mobile phones are largely to blame. Popular prediction markets are also now feeding the frenzy. The industry’s main argument is that online wagering will simply wind up overseas or controlled by organized crime networks if governments don’t legalize it. There’s some basis for such theories, including Australia’s experience with high excise rates pushing tobacco trade onto the black market. Major inconvenience and risks of offshore options would dissuade many casual bettors, however. What’s more, stiff restrictions on advertising, sponsorship, game design, lending and stake limits would go a long way to protect users. In Britain, where gambling is deeply woven into the culture, new rules designed to fit the digital age, aim to stop companies from being allowed to put profit ahead of protection. As communities and politicians start to fully appreciate related financial and health repercussions, outright shutdowns like Brazil’s will garner greater consideration. Prohibition-era bootlegging continues to captivate the public imagination but often lost to collective memory is that temperance was a powerful political movement that overcame deep-pocketed distillers. Booze consumption, along with death rates from alcoholism and cirrhosis, declined steeply under the Volstead Act, and decades went by before they reached early-1900s levels again. Sweeping bans on betting remain a long-shot, but the odds just improved. Follow Jeffrey Goldfarb on X and Linkedin . Brazilian President Luiz Inacio Lula da Silva on September 25 banned online betting as he campaigns for reelection in a tight race with opponent Flavio Bolsonaro. The executive order took effect immediately, but it must be approved by Congress within 120 days to stay in force. Lula signed legislation in 2023 establishing rules and explicitly authorizing online games in addition to sports betting. Licensed operators have been allowed to offer services nationwide since January 2025, after paying concession fees and meeting regulatory requirements. Although Brazil legalized online betting in 2018 under former President Michel Temer, it had remained largely unregulated. CONTEXT-NEWS

item.title: イスラム過激思想影響とイスラエル首相、フライドバイ機副操縦士 動機不明
item.description:
Alexander Cornwell
[エルサレム １日 ロイター] -
item.dc:creator: ロイター
item.content:encoded:
Alexander Cornwell

[エルサレム １日 ロイター] - イスラエル当局者は１日、イスラエルに向かっていた航空機墜落を狙った疑いのある事件について、動機はまだ特定されていないと明らかにした。機長を刺した副操縦士は単独で行動したとみられるという。

ドバイ発テルアビブ行きのフライドバイ機で前日に起きた事件では、負傷した機長が操縦室のドアを解錠したことで惨事が回避された。乗客が襲撃者を取り押さえ、機内にいた交代要員の乗務員が操縦しサウジアラビアに緊急着陸した。

イスラエルのネタニヤフ首相は１日のＦＯＸニュースのインタビューで、副操縦士はイスラム主義思想の影響で過激化していたと指摘。イランとつながりがあるかは数日以内に明らかにできるとし、「判断するのは時期尚早だと思う」と述べた。

また、現時点で得られている情報から副操縦士に自殺願望があったことは明らかとした上で、「最終的な結論は出していない」と語った。

イスラエルの安全保障当局者２人は、副操縦士は単独で行動した可能性が高いとみているが、なお捜査中だと述べた。現時点でイランの関与は特定していないという。

ＵＡＥの国営通信は１日、同国が捜査を開始したと伝えた。事件の状況や動機を明らかにし、「何らかのテロ活動や目的と関連しているのか、あるいは事前の計画や指示があったのか」を調べるという。またＵＡＥの航空会社で機体も登録されていることから、同国が事件の管轄権を持つという。国外で発生した場合でも機内で行われた犯罪にはＵＡＥの法律が適用されるとしている。

item.title: Des frappes aériennes pakistanaises font neuf morts en Afghanistan, selon les taliban
item.description: Des frappes aériennes pakistanaises sur l'Afghanistan ont fait neuf morts jeudi, a déclaré le gouvernement taliban, tandis qu'Islamabad a affirmé avoir tué 22 "terroristes".
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Des frappes aériennes pakistanaises sur l'Afghanistan ont fait neuf morts jeudi, a déclaré le gouvernement taliban, tandis qu'Islamabad a affirmé avoir tué 22 "terroristes". Ces bombardements marquent une escalade dans les combats entre les deux pays voisins après trois mois de calme relatif. Parmi les personnes tuées lors des frappes menées dans les provinces afghanes de Kunar et d'Helmand figurent des femmes et des enfants, a déclaré le porte-parole des taliban, Zabihullah Mujahid, sur le réseau social X, ajoutant que 11 personnes avaient été blessées. "Nous condamnons cet acte, que nous qualifions d’agression et de crime en violation de tous les principes reconnus", a-t-il ajouté. La Mission d’assistance des Nations unies en Afghanistan (MANUA) a indiqué qu’au moins 10 civils avaient été tués lors de ces frappes, dont la plupart étaient des enfants, et que neuf autres avaient été blessés. Le ministère pakistanais de l’Information a déclaré que ces frappes reposaient sur des "renseignements fiables" et visaient des caches de "terroristes" dans deux endroits différents. "Les cibles ont été détruites avec précision et les premiers rapports font état de la mort de 22 terroristes", a-t-il indiqué dans un communiqué publié sur X. "De grandes quantités d’armes et de munitions stockées dans ces repaires ont également été détruites", a-t-il ajouté. Reuters n’a pu vérifier ces informations de manière indépendante. Une attaque menée par des hommes armés contre un poste de police dans le nord-ouest du Pakistan le mois dernier, qui a fait 24 morts, a ravivé les tensions entre le Pakistan et l’Afghanistan. Islamabad accuse Kaboul d’abriter des "terroristes" qui mènent des attaques transfrontalières. Le gouvernement taliban nie ces accusations et affirme que le terrorisme est un problème interne au Pakistan.

item.title: Apenas 13% das empresas avançam em IA diante de barreiras regulatórias e sistemas de TI antigos
item.description: Apenas 13% das empresas estavam no caminho certo com suas iniciativas de IA, já que obstáculos regulatórios e a integração com sistemas de TI antigos retardaram a adoção em larga escala, segundo um estudo da BearingPoint.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Apenas 13% das empresas estavam no caminho certo com suas iniciativas de IA, já que obstáculos regulatórios e a integração com sistemas de TI antigos retardaram a adoção em larga escala, segundo um estudo da BearingPoint. Quase três quartos das empresas pesquisadas relataram resultados financeiros positivos com a IA, mas menos de um terço conseguiu ir além dos projetos-piloto, informou a consultoria nesta quinta-feira. “A IA ultrapassou um limiar importante”, disse o especialista da BearingPoint, Frederic Gigant, acrescentando que comprovar o valor e ampliá-lo são duas coisas diferentes. Cerca de 40% dos entrevistados citaram as regulamentações legais como a principal barreira para a ampliação da IA, enquanto 34% apontaram os desafios de integrar a nova tecnologia aos sistemas de TI existentes. Perto de 24% das empresas relataram economias de custo impulsionadas pela IA de pelo menos 10%, em comparação com apenas 4% que relataram crescimento de receita na mesma proporção. Além disso, quase dois terços das empresas estimaram um excesso de pessoal de pelo menos 10%. A China e os EUA lideram a adoção da IA, com 20% e 18% das empresas relatando implementação abrangente, contra 8% na Alemanha. Já a proporção de empresas com IA profundamente integrada às operações subiu de 7% em 2025 para 11% em 2026.

item.title: Water contamination and cancer concerns
item.description: Hello!
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Hello! Today’s newsletter highlights three separate stories from the United States, Madagascar and Cuba. They all have one thing in common - contamination. We’ll look at how Iowa's soaring cancer rates have become a campaign issue ahead of November’s midterm elections. Many voters fear that the state's worsening water pollution from nitrates and other chemicals may be to blame for a spike in cases. Then we’ll unpack a legal showdown pitting more than 6,500 people in Madagascar against mining group Rio Tinto. The islanders have filed a claim in London’s High Court, alleging that contamination from the company's mineral sands operation exposed them to dangerous levels of lead and uranium. Meanwhile, health authorities in Cuba have warned in recent days of the spread of viruses, including a strain of viral hepatitis, as power and water increasingly fail. * Cancer concerns and contaminated water Iowa's rising cancer rate - the second highest in the US behind Kentucky - has emerged as a major campaign issue ahead of this year’s vote. A Reuters review of campaign materials showed that every major candidate in Iowa's [USN:L4N42Y0N6 TEXT:"competitive races"] for Congress and the state governorship has talked about their plans to tackle cancer in speeches and online posts. Candidates have pledged a range of actions from increasing cancer screening to improving water quality monitoring. It is one of just three states where cases are rising, driven by higher rates of lung, prostate and breast cancers, among others, according to the National Cancer Institute at the National Institutes of Health. Many Iowans tie their cancer concerns to high nitrate levels in the state's water, which can occur when fertilizer washes into rivers and groundwater. About 85% of Iowa is farmland, much of it dedicated to fertilizer-heavy crops such as corn, according to the US Department of Agriculture. The concentration of nitrates in Iowa's main waterways doubled over the past 50 years and regularly exceeds levels set by the Environmental Protection Agency, according to a 2025 statewide report commissioned by Iowa's Polk County Board of Supervisors. Scientists have not reached a consensus on the cancer risk posed by nitrate-contaminated drinking water. Some studies, including by the University of Iowa and the National Cancer Institute, have found associations with higher cancer rates or mortality, while others have not. [USN:L6N44F10S TEXT:"Click here"] to find out more about Iowa’s cancer concerns and the possible links between the disease, contaminated water and pesticides. * Rio Tinto acidic wastewater case Over in Britain, a lawsuit has been brought by [USN:L1N45M0AS TEXT:"community groups from Madagascar"] who live near Rio Tinto's QIT Madagascar Minerals (QMM) mine. According to law firm Leigh Day, which is representing the claimants, the community groups allege that acidic wastewater containing uranium, lead and other metals was discharged into lakes and waterways used for drinking, cooking, washing and irrigation. The mine, which is 80%-owned by Rio Tinto, produces ilmenite, which is processed into titanium dioxide, a white pigment used in products including paint, food and toothpaste. Rio Tinto said it had been notified of the claim but had not yet received details, so could not comment further at the moment. * Clinics without water In Cuba, power outages exacerbated by a US oil blockade have crippled the already crumbling infrastructure that supplies water to Havana's nearly 2 million people. Many regularly go without running water for days or weeks. Healthcare worker Yuamilka Hechavarria told Reuters how she had been forced to buy water from street vendors or scavenge it from broken pipes. [USN:L1N45H0OH TEXT:"Click here"] for the full story to find out more about how local clinics are struggling to cope without water. * Talking Points Thailand floods: The [USN:L6N45L05A TEXT:"death toll from rains and flooding"] in Thailand rose to 23, authorities said, as waters receded from the hard-hit capital Bangkok. The city's governor, Chadchart Sittipunt, said he expected floodwater to drain away from major roads within two days, though it will take up to a week for other inundated areas to be cleared out. US climate litigation: Officials in Boulder, Colorado are seeking to hold major oil companies liable for helping drive climate change and misleading the public about the risks of fossil fuels in a Supreme Court case set to be argued on October 5. The case could determine the fate of dozens of climate-related lawsuits by state and local governments against fossil fuel companies. [USN:L1N45G0O2 TEXT:"Click here"] to learn more about their arguments. UK climate rollbacks: The [USN:L6N45M0QL TEXT:"Financial Conduct Authority"], Britain's financial regulator, has dropped plans to require listed companies to inform investors about their climate risks after firms raised concerns about implementation costs and competitiveness. The move follows steps by the European Union to water down its flagship corporate climate disclosure regime. EU methane rules: The European Commission is considering a postponement of the EU's methane emissions rules for oil and gas imports – set out in the world's first law targeting methane emissions from imported fossil fuels – after calls from France, the US and other governments that said the rules could undermine energy security. [USN:L8N45K07G TEXT:"Click here"] for an explainer on the rules. Ghana illegal mining crackdown: Ghana, Africa's biggest gold producer, has tightened oversight of its mining sector to boost revenue, increase local participation and strengthen compliance, a senior regulator said. [USN:L8N45J070 TEXT:"Click here"] to find out more about the mining companies that have been fined and investigated for environmental breaches and compliance issues linked to illegal gold mining activity. * ESG Spotlight Today’s spotlight showcases a British startup that is turning waste into fertilizer. Meet NPK Recovery , a company that collects urine from event toilets and processes it into a liquid fertilizer containing nitrogen, phosphorus and potassium, using its "pee-cycle" technology. Today’s Sustainable Switch was edited by Andrew Heavens Think your friend or colleague should know about us? Forward this newsletter to them. They can also subscribe here.

item.title: La Russie expulse des diplomates hongrois en guise de représailles
item.description: La Russie prévoit d'expulser un nombre non précisé de diplomates hongrois, a déclaré jeudi le ministère des Affaires étrangères russe, une mesure de rétorsion en réponse à la décision prise le mois dernier par Budapest de renvoyer dix diplomates russes.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: La Russie prévoit d'expulser un nombre non précisé de diplomates hongrois, a déclaré jeudi le ministère des Affaires étrangères russe, une mesure de rétorsion en réponse à la décision prise le mois dernier par Budapest de renvoyer dix diplomates russes. "À titre de mesure de rétorsion, un groupe de membres du personnel de l'ambassade de Hongrie à Moscou et des consulats généraux de Hongrie à Saint-Pétersbourg et à Kazan doit quitter le territoire de la Fédération de Russie dans un délai de deux semaines", a précisé le ministère. Le ministère des Affaires étrangères hongrois dit dans un communiqué prendre acte de la décision russe, ajoutant : "La Hongrie n'a aucun intérêt à voir s'aggraver les tensions diplomatiques". Budapest avait accusé les [USN:L8N45011O TEXT:"diplomates"] russes d'avoir agi d'une manière incompatible avec leur statut — une formulation souvent utilisée comme euphémisme pour désigner l'espionnage. Ces expulsions étaient la bonne illustration du revirement de la politique de la Hongrie vis-à-vis de la Russie depuis que l'ancien Premier ministre Viktor Orban a dû quitter le pouvoir en avril à la suite de sa défaite électorale aux législatives après 16 années à la tête du gouvernement. Malgré l'invasion à grande échelle de l'Ukraine par la Russie en février 2022, Viktor Orban s'était distingué au sein de l'Union européenne en continuant à entretenir des liens étroits avec le président russe Vladimir Poutine. La Hongrie a aussi continué à acheter du pétrole et du gaz russe, a entravé les sanctions européennes contre la Russie et a tenté de bloquer un prêt de 90 milliards d'euros de l'UE à l'Ukraine. Le nouveau chef du gouvernement hongrois, Peter Magyar, et ses ministres ne cessent de répéter que les principales alliances de la Hongrie sont nouées avec l'UE et l'Otan, deux institutions avec lesquelles ils entendent restaurer une confiance ébranlée sous Viktor Orban.

item.title: Ibovespa abre outubro sem viés claro com eleição no horizonte
item.description: O Ibovespa começava outubro sem um viés claro nesta quinta-feira, em meio ao clima de expectativa para o desfecho do primeiro turno das eleições no Brasil.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: O Ibovespa começava outubro sem um viés claro nesta quinta-feira, em meio ao clima de expectativa para o desfecho do primeiro turno das eleições no Brasil. Às 10h10, o índice de referência do mercado acionário brasileiro (.BVSP) registrava variação positiva de 0,04%, a 186.418,35 pontos. O contrato futuro do Ibovespa com vencimento mais curto , em 14 de outubro, recuava 0,29%.

item.title: China driving worrying rise in EU imports, Commission official says
item.description: Nearly a quarter of imports into the European Union are rising at a "worrying" rate, driven primarily by goods from China, the European Commission's chief trade enforcement officer said on Thursday.
item.dc:creator: Philip Blenkinsop
item.content:encoded: Nearly a quarter of imports into the European Union are rising at a "worrying" rate, driven primarily by goods from China, the European Commission's chief trade enforcement officer said on Thursday. Denis Redonnet told the European Parliament that sectors facing sustained and abnormal import growth included machinery, textiles, basic metals and chemicals. Redonnet was addressing the parliament's trade committee as the Commission intensifies discussions with Beijing to address the EU's goods trade deficit with China of €360 billion ($407 billion) in 2025. Chinese imports into the bloc have been rising while EU exports to China have fallen by a similar rate, and Brussels [USN:S8N3US031 TEXT:"hopes to agree"] some form of Chinese export management this month. "It is of serious concern that the import surveillance or barometer results... show potentially worrying trends for almost a quarter of all imports into the EU at the moment," Redonnet said. "And China and Chinese origin is the main driver of these import increases." EU imports totalled €2.53 trillion ($2.86 trillion) in 2025, with €571 billion from China. The increased exports have driven a sharp increase in industry requests for trade defence measures. The EU executive Commission launched 32 new cases in 2025, just off the 2024 record of 33 and compared to a previous historical annual average of 12. More than a third of new investigations involved the chemicals sector. Redonnet said 27 new cases had already been opened in 2026. ($1 = 0.8854 euros)

item.title: Netanjahu: Copilot von Flydubai-Maschine war islamistisch radikalisiert
item.description: Der Copilot des außerplanmäßig gelandeten Flydubai-Jets war nach Angaben des israelischen Ministerpräsidenten Benjamin Netanjahu islamistisch radikalisiert. "Wir wissen, dass er islamistisch-radikal indoktriniert wurde", sagte Netanjahu am Donnerstag in einem Interview mit dem US-Sender Fox News. Zudem sei der Mann offenbar suizidgefährdet gewesen. Die Kombination aus der psychischen Verfassung und der Radikalisierung liefere einen deutlichen Hinweis auf das Motiv, erklärte der Regierungschef. Abschließende Erkenntnisse lägen jedoch noch nicht vor.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Der Copilot des außerplanmäßig gelandeten Flydubai-Jets war nach Angaben des israelischen Ministerpräsidenten Benjamin Netanjahu islamistisch radikalisiert. "Wir wissen, dass er islamistisch-radikal indoktriniert wurde", sagte Netanjahu am Donnerstag in einem Interview mit dem US-Sender Fox News. Zudem sei der Mann offenbar suizidgefährdet gewesen. Die Kombination aus der psychischen Verfassung und der Radikalisierung liefere einen deutlichen Hinweis auf das Motiv, erklärte der Regierungschef. Abschließende Erkenntnisse lägen jedoch noch nicht vor. Bei dem Vorfall am Mittwoch auf dem Flydubai-Flug FZ1073 von Dubai nach Tel Aviv hatte der Copilot den Flugkapitän mit einem Messer angegriffen und wollte den Jet offenbar zum Absturz bringen. Passagiere konnten den Copiloten überwältigen. Eine Ersatzbesatzung an Bord landete die Maschine daraufhin in Saudi-Arabien sicher. Netanjahu erklärte, er wolle nicht über mögliche Verbindungen des Mannes zum Iran oder zu anderen Akteuren spekulieren. "Ich denke, es ist zu früh, um zu sagen, ob er Verbindungen zum Iran oder zu anderen hatte", sagte er. Er gehe jedoch davon aus, in einigen Tagen Klarheit darüber zu gewinnen.

item.title: TSE confirma decisões que removeram postagens sobre Nossa Senhora Aparecida
item.description: O Tribunal Superior Eleitoral (TSE) confirmou na quarta-feira decisões do ministro André Mendonça que haviam determinado a remoção do ar de publicações em redes sociais que relacionavam o senador Flávio Bolsonaro, candidato do PL à Presidência, a um suposto movimento de retirada de Nossa Senhora Aparecida do posto de padroeira do Brasil.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: O Tribunal Superior Eleitoral (TSE) confirmou na quarta-feira decisões do ministro André Mendonça que haviam determinado a remoção do ar de publicações em redes sociais que relacionavam o senador Flávio Bolsonaro, candidato do PL à Presidência, a um suposto movimento de retirada de Nossa Senhora Aparecida do posto de padroeira do Brasil. A maioria dos ministros seguiu o voto de Mendonça que argumentou que suas decisões não tinham qualquer interesse em restringir liberdade religiosa, não constituem censura prévia e foram tomadas de forma excepcional. "Os comandos (decisões) devem ser compreendidos dentro desses exatos limites: não constituem censura prévia; não autorizam proibição temática; não importam suspensão de perfis, contas ou canais; não alcançam críticas ou opiniões que não reproduzam o núcleo factual delimitado; e, em caso de dúvida razoável quanto à equivalência substancial de determinada publicação, a preservação da liberdade de expressão recomenda a manutenção do conteúdo, facultada a submissão da questão ao juízo para esclarecimento", destacou Mendonça, em seu voto. Ao longo do julgamento virtual, Mendonça fez um ajuste de voto para liberar uma publicação do humorista Antonio Tabet sobre o tema. O caso gerou uma grande polêmica por ter repercutido bastante nas redes sociais nas vésperas do primeiro turno da eleição presidencial, no próximo domingo, e levado também a um novo embate entre ministros do Supremo Tribunal Federal. O ministro Flávio Dino, do STF, deu uma decisão cassando a liminar de Mendonça, que atua nos dois tribunais. Em seguida, o ministro Luiz Fux, também do Supremo, cassou a ordem de Dino, restabelecendo a determinação de Mendonça. O presidente do STF, Edson Fachin, chegou a cogitar levar o debate ao plenário do Supremo, mas recuou e deixou para que o TSE tomasse uma decisão colegiada sobre o tema.

item.title: What is in France's 2027 budget?
item.description: French Prime Minister Sebastien Lecornu's government delivered its 2027 budget on Thursday, including a package of measures meant to get its deficit-reduction plans on track with targeted savings and tax increases.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: French Prime Minister Sebastien Lecornu's government delivered [USN:L1N45N0A3 TEXT:"its 2027 budget"] on Thursday, including a package of measures meant to get its deficit-reduction plans on track with targeted savings and tax increases. The following are the main new measures in the bill that was sent to lawmakers, who will likely amend the legislation substantially in parliament in the coming weeks. MAIN TAX MEASURES Employer payroll contributions: A reduction in a tax break employers get on low and mid-level salaries if their employees receive bonuses such as profit-sharing or incentive schemes. It would raise about €3.8 billion ($4.29 billion) in 2027. A freeze on tax relief on low-wage payroll contributions, to raise €2.9 billion. Pensions: A €3,000 cap on a tax break for retirees' professional expenses, to raise €1.4 billion. Motorway concessions: An increase in a tax on long-distance transport infrastructure, which could raise about €800 million more per year. Sugar tax: An extension on a levy on sweetened drinks to include ultra-processed foods high in sugar, to bring in €300 million. SPENDING Pensions: Those over €1,260 a month will not be increased in line with inflation, saving €4.1 billion. A reduction in a tax break that retirees receive for professional expenses, to bring in another €1.4 billion. Health spending: Measures, including cuts to medicine prices, to keep it in check and save about €4 billion. Sick pay: Reforms to allowances made to workers when they are on sick leave, aimed at saving €1 billion. A lowering in the ceiling on sick pay for work accidents, to generate €800 million in savings. ($1 = 0.8854 euros)

item.title: Volantis raises $88 million for tech to connect AI, memory chips
item.description: San Francisco-based semiconductor startup Volantis on Thursday said it has raised $88 million in venture capital in an effort to solve a key challenge for AI chips by tapping a technology that is already sitting in hundreds of millions of iPhones.
item.dc:creator: Stephen Nellis
item.content:encoded: San Francisco-based semiconductor startup Volantis on Thursday said it has raised $88 million in venture capital in an effort to solve a key challenge for AI chips by tapping a technology that is already sitting in hundreds of millions of iPhones. The fundamental limit for AI chips from both Nvidia (NVDA.O) and rivals like Advanced Micro Devices (AMD.O) is how well the computing parts of a chip can talk to the memory chips where an AI model lives and feeds data to the computing chip. Nvidia and AMD solve the problem by encircling their computing chips with [USN:L4N43B15I TEXT:"expensive high-bandwidth memory chips"]. But even Nvidia's best current offerings can hold only eight of those memory chips for each of its graphics processing units (GPUs) because of the limited reach of the tiny electrical wires that connect the memory chips. Volantis says it is developing a way to send data between computing chips and memory chips using beams of laser light, which eliminates the reach problem and would let it pack 220 memory chips around a GPU. To do that, Volantis is tapping what are called vertical-cavity surface-emitting lasers, or VCSELs. While the tiny lasers sound exotic, they power the facial recognition features in many devices from Apple, which [USN:KBN1E804T TEXT:"invested heavily in bolstering the supply chain"] over the past decade. By bringing together relatively well-known components, Volantis is hoping to avoid some of the [USN:L4N3ZQ194 TEXT:"supply chain"] [USN:L6N40C08W TEXT:"bottlenecks"] in developing AI chips and deliver a chip next year that would speed up tasks like AI coding, said Tapa Ghosh, CEO and co-founder of Volantis, in an interview. "Advanced packaging is always to be respected - it's never trivial - but it's not necessarily a new thing to do," Ghosh said. "No one is going to win a Nobel Prize if our project works, but the good news is, they won't need to." The funding round was led by Stripe veteran Lachy Groom and Abstract Ventures. John Doerr, who backed Google and Amazon.com in their early days, also participated, as did VXI Capital, Triatomic and Susa Ventures. The round also includes angel investments from AI podcaster Dwarkesh Patel, AI chip veteran Naveen Rao and Anthropic researcher Sholto Douglas.

item.title: Alumnos escapan ilesos de ataque de drones rusos contra escuela en Kiev
item.description: Unos drones rusos se estrellaron contra una escuela de Kiev y la incendiaron el jueves por la mañana, pero todos los alumnos se encontraban en un refugio en ese momento y no hubo heridos, informaron las autoridades de la capital ucraniana.
item.dc:creator: Dan Peleschuk
item.content:encoded: Unos drones rusos se estrellaron contra una escuela de Kiev y la incendiaron el jueves por la mañana, pero todos los alumnos se encontraban en un refugio en ese momento y no hubo heridos, informaron las autoridades de la capital ucraniana. Un puente sobre el río Dniéper también fue alcanzado en el marco de los ataques cada vez más intensos de Rusia contra la ciudad, dijo el alcalde Vitali Klitschko. El Puente del Sur no sufrió daños importantes, pero se interrumpió temporalmente el tráfico del metro que lo cruza. En la escuela, los equipos de rescate registraban los escombros cerca del edificio carbonizado, cuyas ventanas quedaron destrozadas. Imágenes de las cámaras de seguridad verificadas por Reuters mostraban una brillante bola de fuego que estallaba tras el impacto del dron contra la tercera planta del edificio. "Esos canallas rusos siguen atacando la vida en todo nuestro país, a los niños ucranianos y a nuestras escuelas", dijo el presidente Volodímir Zelenski en la red social X. "Rusia debe rendir cuentas por ello y recibir una respuesta a sus ataques". Los ataques forman parte de una campaña de bombardeos aéreos ininterrumpidos contra Kiev y otras ciudades ucranianas, en la que Rusia ha estado utilizando drones propulsados por reactores, que Ucrania ha tenido dificultades para derribar debido a la falta de defensas aéreas. El miércoles, las fuerzas rusas lanzaron lo que las autoridades ucranianas describieron como el inicio de una campaña de ataques en plena temporada de frío contra la red eléctrica de Ucrania. Estos ataques suponen una escalada destinada a aprovechar la debilidad de la defensa aérea de Ucrania, escribió el analista político Vadym Denysenko en Facebook. El Instituto de Investigación Nuclear de Kiev afirmó en un comunicado que fue alcanzado por un dron a última hora del miércoles, pero que los niveles de radiación se mantenían normales. El lunes, un dron ruso se estrelló contra la Academia Nacional de Ciencias, en el centro de Kiev, causando un muerto y varios heridos.

item.title: Mulher condenada à morte no Tennessee sobrevive a tentativa de execução
item.description: Christa Pike, condenada pelo assassinato de uma colega de escola há três décadas, sobreviveu a uma tentativa do Tennessee de executá-la por meio de injeção letal na noite de quarta-feira, segundo autoridades prisionais, frustrando a primeira tentativa do Estado de executar uma mulher em dois séculos.
item.dc:creator: Steve Gorman
item.content:encoded: Christa Pike, condenada pelo assassinato de uma colega de escola há três décadas, sobreviveu a uma tentativa do Tennessee de executá-la por meio de injeção letal na noite de quarta-feira, segundo autoridades prisionais, frustrando a primeira tentativa do Estado de executar uma mulher em dois séculos. A condição de saúde de Pike após o incidente não foi divulgada imediatamente, e não ficou claro quais medidas legais seus advogados ou o Estado poderão tomar a seguir, depois que ela foi transferida da Instituição de Segurança Máxima Riverbend, em Nashville, para receber tratamento médico. O Departamento Penitenciário do Tennessee defendeu a forma como conduziu a execução de grande repercussão, que havia sido contestada por seus advogados e especialistas em direitos humanos devido à idade de Pike na época do crime, seu histórico como vítima de abuso sexual na infância e doença mental não tratada. “O Departamento Penitenciário do Tennessee seguiu todas as etapas do protocolo de execução legal e estabelecido pelo Estado, aprovado pela Procuradoria-Geral”, afirmou a agência em comunicado. “O produto químico da injeção letal previsto no protocolo tem se mostrado consistentemente eficaz, e o protocolo não permite procedimentos adicionais além daqueles realizados nesta noite. Christa Pike foi transportada para um centro médico externo”, concluiu o comunicado. Os advogados de Pike entraram com uma moção na justiça federal durante o processo buscando suspender sua execução, citando relatos de testemunhas de que “os executores haviam injetado ambas as seringas com as substâncias letais e Pike ainda estava viva e roncando”, informou a NBC News. O governador do Tennessee, Bill Lee, que negou o pedido de clemência de Pike na segunda-feira, divulgou um comunicado após a execução fracassada, suspendendo todas as execuções neste ano e solicitando uma “análise abrangente por terceiros” da tentativa de execução de Pike, segundo o Nashville Tennessean. A execução fracassada é a segunda no Tennessee este ano, depois que, em maio, autoridades prisionais interromperam as tentativas de executar um homem condenado por homicídios ao não conseguirem encontrar uma veia adequada para a injeção letal. A tentativa fracassada na quarta-feira ocorreu horas depois que a Suprema Corte dos EUA revogou uma suspensão da execução concedida de última hora por um tribunal de instância inferior, abrindo caminho para que Pike, de 50 anos, fosse executada por seu papel na tortura e morte por espancamento, em 1995, de Colleen Slemmer, de 19 anos, em Knoxville. Pike tinha 18 anos em janeiro de 1995 quando ela, seu namorado Tadaryl Shipp, de 17 anos, e um terceiro companheiro atraíram Slemmer, uma colega de classe do centro profissionalizante Job Corps de Knoxville, para uma área arborizada onde a torturaram e mataram. A natureza macabra do assassinato, que envolveu os perpetradores gravando a forma de um pentagrama no peito da vítima e retirando um pedaço de seu crânio como lembrança do crime, atraiu intensa cobertura da mídia na época. Pike e Shipp confessaram o crime e ambos foram condenados por homicídio doloso qualificado. A mãe de Slemmer, May Martinez, se manifestou a favor da execução. Jornalistas que testemunharam a tentativa de execução descreveram roncos, expirações ruidosas, suspiros e queixas de Pike sobre desconforto no braço. Em alguns momentos, a cortina foi fechada e os jornalistas só podiam ouvir os sons. Segundo eles, clérigos foram chamados à câmara duas vezes antes que uma ambulância fosse vista chegando à prisão e, em seguida, partindo. Além de ser a primeira mulher que o Estado do Tennessee tentou executar em mais de 200 anos, Pike também estava prestes a se tornar a única pessoa na era moderna da pena de morte nos EUA a ser executada no Tennessee por um crime cometido quando era adolescente.

item.title: Iran's Revolutionary Guards kill six "terrorists" in restive region, IRNA news agency reports
item.description: Iran's Revolutionary Guards killed six members of a "terrorist" group on Thursday, the IRNA state news agency reported, in a region often hit by clashes between the security forces and armed groups, including Sunni militants and separatists.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Iran's Revolutionary Guards killed six members of a "terrorist" group on Thursday, the IRNA state news agency reported, in a region often hit by clashes between the security forces and armed groups, including Sunni militants and separatists. The killings occurred in Zahedan, capital of the impoverished Sistan-Baluchistan province in southeastern Iran, which borders Pakistan and Afghanistan and is a major drug trafficking route. The IRNA report said security forces had discovered and confiscated explosive packages. It did not identify the six people killed and gave no further information on the incident. Tehran accuses some armed groups of ties to foreign powers and involvement in cross-border smuggling. Human rights group Haalvsh, which monitors Sistan-Baluchistan, said fighting between military and security forces and armed individuals had started on Thursday morning. Separately, the sound of an explosion was heard on Wednesday in Zahedan without causing any damage, Fars news agency reported, citing the city's administrative office. The reports came as Tehran [USN:S8N43Z002 TEXT:"weighs"] a US response to its latest proposal to revive the collapsed ceasefire in the Gulf and [USN:L8N45M1N4 TEXT:"prepares"] for a possible resumption of large-scale US military attacks after 7 months of conflict that began with US-Israeli attacks on Iran on February 28.

item.title: Solicitudes semanales de subsidio por desempleo caen en EEUU; los despidos se reducen en septiembre
item.description: Las nuevas solicitudes de subsidios por desempleo en Estados Unidos cayeron la semana pasada y los despidos disminuyeron en septiembre, lo que sugiere que la estabilidad del mercado laboral se mantuvo, a pesar de que las empresas siguieron mostrándose cautelosas a la hora de aumentar la contratación.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Las nuevas solicitudes de subsidios por desempleo en Estados Unidos cayeron la semana pasada y los despidos disminuyeron en septiembre, lo que sugiere que la estabilidad del mercado laboral se mantuvo, a pesar de que las empresas siguieron mostrándose cautelosas a la hora de aumentar la contratación. Las solicitudes iniciales de subsidios estatales por desempleo bajaron en 1.000 a 197.000, según cifras ajustadas por estacionalidad, durante la semana que finalizó el 26 de septiembre, informó el jueves el Departamento del Trabajo. Los economistas encuestados por Reuters habían pronosticado 200.000 solicitudes para la última semana. Las solicitudes se sitúan cerca de mínimos de 57 años, a pesar de los crecientes obstáculos derivados de la guerra de Estados Unidos e Israel contra Irán, que está provocando un aumento de los precios de la energía. Los precios del diésel se encuentran en máximos históricos. Los economistas señalaron que el sólido crecimiento de las ganancias empresariales y la resistencia de la demanda interna estaban protegiendo a los trabajadores de los despidos. Otro informe de la consultora internacional de recolocación Challenger, Gray & Christmas reveló que los despidos previstos por las empresas con sede en Estados Unidos descendieron un 18%, a 43.281, en septiembre. Los recortes de empleo anunciados se redujeron un 20% con respecto al año anterior. En lo que va de año, las empresas han anunciado 573.195 despidos, un 39% menos en comparación con los primeros nueve meses de 2025. Los recortes de empleo previstos se redujeron un 43% en el tercer trimestre. Sin embargo, las empresas no tienen prisa por aumentar su plantilla. Los planes de contratación aumentaron en 90.787 el mes pasado. Aunque esto supuso un fuerte repunte respecto a los 12.325 de agosto, las intenciones de contratación se redujeron un 23% con respecto al año anterior, y la cifra fue la más baja registrada en un mes de septiembre desde 2011. Challenger, Gray & Christmas señaló que no se produjo el repunte de la contratación estacional que suele observarse a partir de septiembre. "Las empresas se encuentran ahora mismo en un periodo de espera", dijo Andy Challenger, director de ingresos de Challenger, Gray & Christmas. "Los empleadores se enfrentan a unos elevados costos energéticos, una guerra incierta en Irán, una subida de las tasas de interés que podría encarecer la contratación, además de la probabilidad de que se disparen los costos sanitarios". El mes pasado, la Reserva Federal elevó su tasa de interés de referencia a un día en 25 puntos básicos, situándola en el rango del 3,75%-4,00%, en la primera alza en tres años, y apuntó a que podrían producirse nuevas subidas de los costos de financiación en los próximos meses. El informe sobre solicitudes de subsidio de desempleo mostró que el número de personas que recibían prestaciones tras la primera semana de ayuda, un indicador de la contratación, descendió en 11.000 hasta 1,701 millones, según cifras ajustadas estacionalmente, durante la semana que finalizó el 19 de septiembre. Aunque las denominadas "solicitudes continuas" se sitúan en el extremo inferior de su rango para este año, algunas personas que han perdido su empleo están atravesando largos períodos de desempleo. Una encuesta del Conference Board publicada el martes reveló que la proporción de consumidores que afirmaban que había "abundancia de empleo" descendió en septiembre a su nivel más bajo desde febrero de 2021, mientras que la proporción de quienes consideraban que era "difícil conseguir trabajo" alcanzó su nivel más alto en más de cinco años y medio. Los datos sobre las solicitudes de subsidio no influyen en el informe de empleo de septiembre, ya que quedan fuera del periodo de la encuesta. Es probable que el empleo no agrícola haya aumentado en 90.000 puestos de trabajo el mes pasado, tras haber registrado un incremento de 162.000 en agosto, según una encuesta de Reuters a economistas. Se prevé que la tasa de desempleo se mantenga estable en el 4,1% por tercer mes consecutivo, aunque los riesgos apuntan a un repunte.

item.title: Contração da indústria no Brasil se intensifica em setembro com demanda fraca, mostra PMI
item.description: A atividade industrial brasileira afundou ainda mais em terreno contracionista em setembro e atingiu o nível mais baixo em quase três anos e meio, com um forte enfraquecimento da demanda, de acordo com a pesquisa Índice de Gerentes de Compras (PMI) divulgada nesta quinta-feira.
item.dc:creator: Camila Moreira
item.content:encoded: A atividade industrial brasileira afundou ainda mais em terreno contracionista em setembro e atingiu o nível mais baixo em quase três anos e meio, com um forte enfraquecimento da demanda, de acordo com a pesquisa Índice de Gerentes de Compras (PMI) divulgada nesta quinta-feira. Segundo a pesquisa, a fraqueza da demanda, as pressões competitivas e a incerteza política antes das eleições presidenciais de outubro pesaram sobre as vendas, enquanto o aumento dos custos agravou o ambiente desafiador para os negócios. Ainda assim, a confiança para os próximos 12 meses melhorou em relação a agosto. O PMI da indústria, compilado pela S&P Global, caiu a 44,8 em setembro, de 46,3 em agosto, na maior deterioração das condições operacionais desde abril de 2023. A marca de 50 separa crescimento de contração. O resultado levou a média trimestral a 46,2, a mais baixa desde o segundo trimestre de 2023, segundo a S&P Global. “O único aspecto positivo nos dados do PMI foi que as empresas continuaram mais otimistas em relação aos próximos 12 meses, amparadas pela expectativa de que as condições de mercado melhorem após as eleições”, avaliou Pollyanna De Lima, diretora associada de economia da S&P Global Market Intelligence. A retração da produção chegou ao quinto mês consecutivo e se intensificou para o nível mais forte desde o início da pandemia de Covid-19, no começo de 2020. Os participantes da pesquisa associaram a queda da produção à fraqueza das vendas, ao aumento dos custos dos insumos e às incertezas relacionadas ao período pré-eleitoral. As entradas de novos pedidos sofreram o maior ritmo de contração em quase quatro anos. As novas encomendas do exterior diminuíram pelo quinto mês seguido, embora o ritmo de contração tenha desacelerado em relação a agosto. Foram relatadas vendas mais fracas para clientes na Argentina, China, México e Estados Unidos. A indústria brasileira também reduziu em setembro o número de empregados pelo terceiro mês consecutivo, embora o ritmo dos cortes de vagas tenha sido moderado e mais brando do que em agosto. Já os dados de preços mostraram uma retomada das pressões dos custos em setembro. Após desacelerar em cada um dos quatro meses anteriores, a inflação dos preços dos insumos acelerou e voltou a ficar acima de sua média histórica de longo prazo. As empresas atribuíram o aumento dos custos de materiais e transporte à crise global de energia e à guerra no Oriente Médio. Embora os fabricantes tenham voltado a elevar seus preços de venda em resposta, a concorrência e a queda das vendas limitaram seu poder de precificação, e a inflação dos preços cobrados enfraqueceu para o menor nível em sete meses.

item.title: Teachers' strike brings new upheaval for Libyans as school year stalls
item.description: A teachers' strike over pay and working conditions is disrupting schools across Libya and delaying the start of the new academic year.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: A teachers' strike over pay and working conditions is disrupting schools across Libya and delaying the start of the new academic year. Teachers began protesting on September 13, the day schools were due to reopen, staging sit-ins outside schools and government buildings in the capital, Tripoli. Two weeks later, the teachers union escalated the campaign into an open-ended, nationwide strike across public schools. The walkout is the latest upheaval in a country still grappling with instability years after the 2011 NATO-backed uprising that toppled Muammar Gaddafi. Libya has also faced [USN:L6N4590IX TEXT:"widespread power cuts"] this summer and labour unrest that recently disrupted output at its largest oilfield. Teachers say low salaries and deteriorating school conditions have pushed them to act. "These are not demands, but rather rights – and rights have to be taken," said Mustafa Al-Bahilil, head of the teachers union in Ain Zara on Tripoli's southern outskirts. Teachers face difficulties ranging from a lack of computer labs to desks so worn out that they are unusable, often forcing staff and parents to pay for equipment themselves. Many teachers have to work second jobs because their salaries are so low, said Tripoli teacher Hamza al-Firjani. "They get promises, but all of them are fake promises," he said. The Ministry of Education did not immediately respond to a Reuters request for an interview. Teachers have also joined the strike in Benghazi in eastern Libya. The country has been divided between rival administrations in the east and west since a 2014 civil war. Mohammed Al-Jahawi, head of the teachers union in Benghazi, said the strikes were driven by surging food and other costs which had left many teachers unable to meet their basic needs. The prospect of a long disruption has left many parents anxious. Salah Awad, a 47-year-old father of three students in Benghazi, said he hoped that the teachers' needs were addressed, but he feared the strike was going to hurt students. "This is not the right time for a strike," he said.

item.title: If a bruising third quarter can’t halt Wall Street, what can?
item.description: Wednesday closed the books on an extraordinary quarter. A 40% rebound in Brent crude oil, record-high diesel prices, bond yields at 20-year highs and AI's threat to wipe out humanity gave investors no shortage of reasons to retrench. Yet faced with that formidable wall of worry, US and world stocks still scaled fresh record highs.
item.dc:creator: Jamie McGeever
item.content:encoded: Wednesday closed the books on an extraordinary quarter. A 40% rebound in Brent crude oil, [USN:L1N45G0Q3 TEXT:"record-high diesel prices"], [USN:L1N45K0MU TEXT:"bond yields"] at 20-year highs and AI's threat to [USN:L4N45K1J5 TEXT:"wipe out humanity"] gave investors no shortage of reasons to retrench. Yet faced with that formidable wall of worry, US and world stocks still scaled fresh record highs. Equities weren't exactly booming. The S&P 500 (.SPX) rose only 2%. But considering the dismal backdrop and the fact that the third quarter followed the strongest three-month period in six years, that’s not too shabby. Only last month, the S&P 500 and MSCI All Country World index (.MIWD00000PUS) were at their peaks, while the tech-heavy Nasdaq (.IXIC) traded at a new high of 27,288 points just last week. Wall Street's Teflon-like qualities have been something to behold. That is largely thanks to corporate earnings growth in the second quarter, which came in at a stunning 53.7%. Of course, it's a little murkier under the surface. Around 40% of S&P 500 stocks are down for the year, and a quarter of the index's constituents have fallen 10% or more, according to Ben Carlson at Ritholtz Wealth Management. Strategists at Goldman Sachs reckon market breadth is the narrowest since 2000. A handful of tech giants are boosting an otherwise middling market, with AI increasingly the only game in town. More than half of the S&P 500's market capitalization is now composed of AI or AI-adjacent companies. The global equity picture was more mixed than in the US, with benchmark indices in Japan (.N225) , China (.SSEC) and Europe (.STOXX) losing ground. None gave up as much as South Korea's KOSPI (.KS11) , which tumbled around 20%. Context is key, though. The tech-heavy Korean index had soared nearly 70% in the previous quarter in a retail-driven AI frenzy that prompted regulators to issue a string of measures to cool the mania. As we begin the final quarter of 2026, the question is whether equities can continue to grind higher. Forecasts for AI- and tech-infused earnings growth remain lofty, but, as the third quarter showed, many of the obstacles in Wall Street's path are just getting bigger. BOND BLUES The most glaring concern is the cost of capital, which is rising – rapidly. The 10-year US Treasury yield , still the world's benchmark borrowing cost against which trillions of dollars of loans are referenced globally, rose more than 85 basis points in the quarter. That's one of its biggest quarterly rises in the last 50 years. Yields across most of the US Treasury curve are at their highest levels since the mid-2000s, and it's a similar story in Europe and Japan. This reflects a major hawkish shift in global interest rate expectations on the back of rising price pressures. The Federal Reserve, under the stewardship of new Chair Kevin Warsh, raised rates in September for the first time in three years. Sovereign bonds are being hit from all sides. Energy supply shocks stemming from the US-Iran and Russia-Ukraine wars are stoking inflation fears. Then there’s the pressure on governments to ramp up spending on defense, energy security and AI infrastructure, despite their precarious fiscal positions. Uncle Sam's finances aren't encouraging, with total US debt crossing the [USN:S0N43F052 TEXT:"$40 trillion barrier"] in August. That appeared to be a manna for crypto investors, who pushed bitcoin up 43% in the July-September period, making the leading cryptocurrency one of the biggest winners across the asset spectrum. Credit, meanwhile, came under heavy pressure. US investment-grade and high-yield corporate bonds racked up their biggest quarterly losses since 2022, according to ICE Bank of America aggregate index data. Much of that can be pinned on the glut of new AI-related borrowing, which is expected to remain strong in the final quarter of the year and rise next year. WHAT'S NEXT? Looking forward, the hawkish rate outlook in the US remains a major headwind. While current market pricing puts the likelihood of an [USN:P8N44M008 TEXT:"October hike at roughly 50%,"] the bond market is indicating the Fed has more work to do. Will the Fed's next step be later this month, just days before the US midterm elections, or in December? Ultimately, it will be difficult for the fourth quarter to match the drama of the last three months, but investors should brace themselves. On top of more expected interest rate rises in the US and around the world, worries about AI's threats to financial stability, the long-term employment outlook and human existence itself are unlikely to fade quickly. The US-Iran war is still raging, too. Can equities shrug all that off again? Investors may get an answer as the third-quarter earnings season kicks into gear in the next few weeks. (The opinions expressed here are those of the author, a columnist for Reuters) Enjoying this column? Check out Reuters Open Interest (ROI), your essential new source for global financial commentary. item.title: Merz wirft Russland "gewalttätigen Revisionismus" vor
item.description: Bundeskanzler Friedrich Merz hat Russland die Bedrohung Europas vorgeworfen. "Heute ist unsere kontinentale Friedensordnung durch den gewalttätigen Revisionismus aus Russland herausgefordert", sagte er am Donnerstag beim Besuch des deutsch-niederländischen Korps in Münster. Moskau habe einen mörderischen Krieg in der Ukraine entfesselt und missachte und verachte Recht und Ordnung. "In der Ukraine steht auch die Sicherheit unseres Teils Europas, in dem wir leben, auf dem Spiel", betonte der Kanzler. Deshalb sei man bereit für eine diplomatische Lösung, auch wenn Moskau nicht an den Verhandlungstisch kommen wolle. Deshalb unterstütze man aber die Ukraine auch gemeinsam in der Nato und "mit aller Kraft". Auch durch Russlands hybride Angriffe auf Europa werde man sich dabei nicht beirren lassen. Man arbeite mit Hochdruck an einer glaubhaften

item.title: Ford to make full factory return to WRC in 2028
item.description: Ford will return to the World Rally Championship (WRC) as a full factory team from 2028 with long-standing partner M-Sport, it announced on Thursday.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Ford will return to the World Rally Championship (WRC) as a full factory team from 2028 with long-standing partner M-Sport, it announced on Thursday. The U.S. marque is the fourth constructor to commit to building a Rally1 car for 2029 under the governing FIA's new WRC27 regulations which are aimed at reducing the cost of competing at the top level. It will be Ford's first full works programme since 2012 in the WRC, which is planning to expand its presence in the US and Britain. "Today’s announcement represents another significant moment for the FIA World Rally Championship," said FIA president Mohammed Ben Sulayem in a statement. "With a [USN:L6N43X14L TEXT:"new promoter in place"], three constructors already committed to the new technical regulations, and now Ford confirming its return as a full works manufacturer, there is real momentum behind the championship’s next era." M-Sport currently competes with Ford Puma cars and has received technical support from Ford since 2012. Before that, it ran the works team. Ford is already involved in Formula One with Red Bull, is set to compete in the World Endurance Championship from 2027 and is present in the World Rally-Raid Championship that includes the annual Dakar Rally in January. Ford cars have won 94 WRC rallies and the previous works team took three manufacturer titles. The manufacturer is trying to revive its fortunes in Europe where Chinese automakers are expanding fast. The company said in May that it will l[USN:L1N41V0AR TEXT:"aunch seven new models"] in Europe by 2029. “Rallying is where Ford’s character faces its toughest test, and where generations of fans come to share the thrill of seeing a car take on the impossible," said Ford Europe president Jim Baumbick on Thursday. "We want our next generation of European vehicles to carry that same unapologetic spirit."

item.title: Latvia's Kulbergs eyes election win as Russia divides society
item.description: Latvia's staunchly pro-Ukraine Prime Minister Andris Kulbergs is likely to retain power after Saturday's national election, as many voters grow wary of potential Russian aggression amid airspace incursions that brought down the previous coalition.
item.dc:creator: Andrius Sytas, Janis Laizans
item.content:encoded: Latvia's staunchly pro-Ukraine Prime Minister Andris Kulbergs is likely to retain power after Saturday's national election, as many voters grow wary of potential Russian aggression amid airspace incursions that [USN:L8N41R0LU TEXT:"brought down the previous coalition"]. Kulbergs, 47, a former racing driver, came to power in May after a previous coalition crumbled over its handling of incidents in which [USN:L1N41K03T TEXT:"stray military drones flew"] undetected into Latvia. Though the drones were Ukrainian, officials [USN:L8N41X1AC TEXT:"have blamed Russia"] for causing them to divert from their flight paths. Baltic officials have warned for months Russia is mounting sabotage, cyber- and other hybrid attacks across Europe to erode support for Ukraine and sow fear, although they dismiss concerns it is capable of launching a direct assault on NATO. Russia says such accusations are baseless and the result of anti-Russian hysteria. Throughout his campaign, Kulbergs has promised "unwavering support to Ukraine" and more anti-drone capabilities for Latvia. Polls open at 8 a.m. (0500 GMT) on Saturday and close at 8 p.m., with the first results expected within hours and the final result likely to be clear after midnight. COALITION-BUILDING LIKELY TO BE DIFFICULT Kulbergs' centrist United List party leads the polls, though with only 14.4% of the vote, and putting a coalition together will likely be a tough task, with seven parties expected to win seats in parliament. "The Ukraine war has divided our society. A lot of people do not share the same outlook," Kulbergs told Reuters in the capital Riga on Wednesday. "A pretty large part of society does not perceive Russia as a threat, they do not understand why the government is investing big money in defence ... They are mistaken." The pro-Russian Sovereign Power, which draws support from Latvia's substantial Russian-speaking minority, is running second in opinion polls with 9.4%. It pledges to stop help to Ukraine's war effort, and its leader Julia Stepanenko refused to state whether she supported economic sanctions on Russia. "Our voters want peace," she told Reuters. Still, pollsters say many Latvians are disenchanted with the country's divisive politics, and one-third say they are undecided or would not vote. The populist Latvia First party, founded by a tycoon with ties to Russian oligarchs, is running third in opinion polls and also appears to have attracted a growing number of pro-Russia voters, with a campaign promising to bridge gaps between ethnic Latvians and Russians. "Latvian Russians are generally pro-Russia, but in the 2022 election, they mostly stayed away, embarrassed by the war," said Arnis Kaktins, a pollster. "If they show up to vote this time, parties with pro-Russian orientation will do well." SOCIETY ON EDGE Latvia, with a population of 1.9 million, is sandwiched between the Baltic Sea and its two European Union and NATO allies Estonia and Lithuania to the north and south, with Russia and Belarus to the east. The precariousness of its geography is clear in Daugavpils, a town of 94,000 located 24 kilometres (15 miles) from Lithuania and 33 km from Belarus. Riga, away on the Baltic shore, feels distant. Ethnic Russians account for about a third of Riga's population and half of residents in Daugavpils, Latvia's second-largest city. Andzela, 59, a music teacher who declined to give her last name, said she lost her job after failing a Latvian language exam. She hopes the next parliament removes the requirement, one of many policies taken since Russia's full-scale invasion of Ukraine in 2022 aimed at limiting the influence of Russia in public life. Her sense of being neglected by policymakers is shared by many, and drives the appeal of Sovereign Power and Latvia First, said local journalist Inna Plavoka. "They tell them: we will save the Russian language, you won't have to learn Latvian, you will be able to go to Russia again for cheap fuel and cheap food," she said. "And let's not give money to Ukraine, give it to elderly people here instead." Daugavpils activist Olga Petkevica said she recently joined Latvia First hoping it becomes a coalition kingmaker and moves Latvia towards a more pragmatic relationship with Russia. "I am not saying Ukraine is bad or Russia is good ... I look at our lives and we are not well... yes, they have war over there, but we live worse here," she said. Back in Riga, Ruta Slavinska, a 60-year-old finance director at an advertising agency, is undecided who she will vote for. "The threat, of course, is simple – a threat to Latvia's freedom."

item.title: Rashid, Curran return as England call up uncapped trio for Pakistan ODI tri-series
item.description: England named spinner Adil Rashid and all-rounder Sam Curran in a 16-man squad on Thursday for this month's one-day tri-series in Pakistan, while uncapped trio Mason Crane, Henry Crocombe and James Coles also earned their first ODI call-ups.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: England named spinner Adil Rashid and all-rounder Sam Curran in a 16-man squad on Thursday for this month's one-day tri-series in Pakistan, while uncapped trio Mason Crane, Henry Crocombe and James Coles also earned their first ODI call-ups. Rashid and Curran return to the squad after recovering from their respective injuries. Leg-spinner Crane, 29, who is uncapped in the ODI format, earns a call-up eight years after his last England appearance. Batter Harry Brook will captain the side but wicketkeeper-batter Jos Buttler misses out with a hamstring injury. Fast bowler Jofra Archer has been rested to manage his workload. The tri-series will be in Lahore and Rawalpindi from October 18 to 31. England face Pakistan and Sri Lanka in the tournament. The top two meet in the final at Lahore's Gaddafi Stadium. ENGLAND SQUAD Harry Brook, Gus Atkinson, Sonny Baker, Tom Banton, James Coles, Jordan Cox, Mason Crane, Henry Crocombe, Sam Curran, Liam Dawson, Ben Duckett, Will Jacks, Jamie Overton, Adil Rashid, Joe Root, Josh Tongue
